# How to translate this chunk

This file holds `items`, a list of `{"k", "ctx", "t"}`. `t` is English text
that a reader of an Indian app or website sees. `ctx` is the field it came
from, such as label, hint, button, documents, brief or title. Use it to judge
tone and length: a label stays short, a hint can be a sentence.

Write `{"items": [{"k": ..., "t": ...}, ...]}` to the path in `write_to`.
Keep every `k` unchanged and in the same order. Put the translation in `t`.
Leave out `ctx`. Do not add, merge, split or drop items.

## Keep these exactly as they are

- Placeholders and markup: `{0}`, `{name}`, `%s`, `%d`, `%1$s`, HTML tags, `\n`.
- Website addresses, e-mail addresses and links.
- Every number: phone and toll-free numbers, Aadhaar, account, IFSC, PAN, PIN
  codes, amounts, dates, percentages. Write digits as 0-9, the Western digits,
  in every language, including Urdu. People type these into forms that take
  Western digits.
- Acronyms people know in Latin letters: OTP, PAN, IFSC, UPI, KYC, e-KYC, DBT,
  BPL, APL, NFSA, PM-KISAN, SMS, PDF, ID.

## Names

- Product, app, portal and scheme names: transliterate them into the script so
  they read naturally. Keep any acronym inside them in Latin, so "APPSC
  portal" becomes APPSC followed by the word for portal.
- A button or menu label quoted from a website, such as 'Apply Online' or
  'Register', stays in English inside quotes. The reader has to find that exact
  English word on the screen.
- People and places in examples are transliterated, never replaced with other
  names.
- Government office titles are transliterated so the reader can say them at
  the counter: Tahsildar, Patwari, Talathi, Mamlatdar, BDO, Collector, Gram
  Panchayat. The language notes below give the usual local forms.

## Tone

Write for an ordinary person who may be elderly and may have had little
schooling. Use everyday spoken language, not heavy official vocabulary. Where
people really say the English word, write it in the script: online, form,
portal, login, mobile, bank, certificate, download, upload, app. Keep
instructions short and direct, in the form "do this".

"Gender" means sex (male or female). It is never the word for caste.

## Before you write

Check that you have the same number of items as the input and that every
number and placeholder came through. Write the whole file in ONE Write call,
as valid UTF-8 JSON with no `\u` escapes and nothing else in the file.

## Hindi (hi)

Script: Devanagari. Used in UP, MP, Bihar, Rajasthan, Haryana, HP, Uttarakhand,
Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Delhi, and understood across the north.
Tone: everyday spoken Hindi (Hindustani). Avoid Sanskritised official words.
Words: ऑनलाइन, फॉर्म, पोर्टल, लॉगिन, आधार, बैंक, मोबाइल, OTP, हेल्पलाइन,
सर्टिफिकेट, डाउनलोड, अपलोड.
UI: आवेदन करें (Apply), जमा करें (Submit), आगे (Next), पीछे (Back), खोजें (Search),
शेयर करें (Share), सेटिंग (Settings), भाषा (Language), मदद (Help).
Offices: तहसीलदार, पटवारी, ग्राम पंचायत, कलेक्टर, ब्लॉक विकास कार्यालय (BDO).
Gender: लिंग (never जाति). Money: रु. 6,000; रु. 8 लाख. September: सितंबर.

## Gujarati (gu)

Script: Gujarati. Used in Gujarat, and spoken in Dadra & Nagar Haveli and
Daman & Diu.
Tone: everyday spoken Gujarati.
Words: ઓનલાઇન, ફોર્મ, પોર્ટલ, લૉગિન, આધાર, બેંક, મોબાઇલ, OTP, હેલ્પલાઇન, સર્ટિફિકેટ / દાખલો,
ડાઉનલોડ, અપલોડ.
UI: અરજી કરો, સબમિટ કરો, આગળ, પાછળ, શોધો, શેર કરો, સેટિંગ્સ, ભાષા, મદદ.
Offices: મામલતદાર, તલાટી, ગ્રામ પંચાયત, કલેક્ટર, તાલુકા પંચાયત.
Gender: જાતિ is caste; use લિંગ. Money: રૂ. 6,000; રૂ. 8 લાખ. September: સપ્ટેમ્બર.

## Marathi (mr)

Script: Devanagari. Used in Maharashtra, and widely in Goa.
Tone: everyday Marathi as spoken in Maharashtra.
Words: ऑनलाइन, फॉर्म, पोर्टल, लॉगिन, आधार, बँक, मोबाइल, OTP, हेल्पलाइन, दाखला / सर्टिफिकेट,
डाउनलोड, अपलोड.
UI: अर्ज करा, सबमिट करा, पुढे, मागे, शोधा, शेअर करा, सेटिंग्ज, भाषा, मदत.
Offices: तहसीलदार, तलाठी, ग्रामपंचायत, जिल्हाधिकारी (कलेक्टर), आपले सरकार सेवा केंद्र.
Gender: लिंग. Money: रु. 6,000; रु. 8 लाख. September: सप्टेंबर.

## Bengali (bn)

Script: Bengali. Used in West Bengal and Tripura, and in Assam's Barak Valley
and the Andamans.
Tone: everyday spoken Bengali (চলিত ভাষা), not সাধু ভাষা.
Words: অনলাইন, ফর্ম, পোর্টাল, লগইন, আধার, ব্যাংক, মোবাইল, OTP, হেল্পলাইন, সার্টিফিকেট,
ডাউনলোড, আপলোড.
UI: আবেদন করুন, জমা দিন, পরবর্তী, পিছনে, খুঁজুন, শেয়ার করুন, সেটিংস, ভাষা, সাহায্য.
Offices: বিডিও অফিস, গ্রাম পঞ্চায়েত, তহসিলদার, জেলাশাসক (কালেক্টর), দুয়ারে সরকার.
Gender: লিঙ্গ. Money: 6,000 টাকা; 8 লাখ টাকা. September: সেপ্টেম্বর.

## Assamese (as)

Script: Bengali script with the Assamese letters ৰ and ৱ. Used in Assam.
This is Assamese, not Bengali. Use Assamese words and spellings: আঁচনি
(scheme), বেংক (bank), কৰক (do), নহয় (is not).
Words: অনলাইন, প্ৰপত্ৰ / ফৰ্ম, পৰ্টেল, লগইন, আধাৰ, বেংক, মবাইল, OTP, হেল্পলাইন, প্ৰমাণপত্ৰ,
ডাউনল'ড, আপল'ড.
UI: আবেদন কৰক, দাখিল কৰক, পৰৱৰ্তী, উভতি যাওক, বিচাৰক, শ্বেয়াৰ কৰক, ছেটিংছ, ভাষা, সহায়.
Offices: চক্ৰ বিষয়াৰ কাৰ্যালয় (Circle Office), গাঁও পঞ্চায়ত, উন্নয়ন খণ্ড কাৰ্যালয় (BDO),
জিলা উপায়ুক্ত.
Gender: লিংগ. Money: 6,000 টকা; 8 লাখ টকা. September: ছেপ্তেম্বৰ.

## Punjabi (pa)

Script: Gurmukhi. Used in Punjab and Chandigarh, and spoken in Delhi and
Haryana.
Tone: everyday spoken Punjabi.
Words: ਆਨਲਾਈਨ, ਫਾਰਮ, ਪੋਰਟਲ, ਲੌਗਇਨ, ਆਧਾਰ, ਬੈਂਕ, ਮੋਬਾਈਲ, OTP, ਹੈਲਪਲਾਈਨ, ਸਰਟੀਫਿਕੇਟ,
ਡਾਊਨਲੋਡ, ਅਪਲੋਡ.
UI: ਅਰਜ਼ੀ ਦਿਓ, ਜਮ੍ਹਾਂ ਕਰੋ, ਅੱਗੇ, ਪਿੱਛੇ, ਖੋਜੋ, ਸਾਂਝਾ ਕਰੋ, ਸੈਟਿੰਗਾਂ, ਭਾਸ਼ਾ, ਮਦਦ.
Offices: ਤਹਿਸੀਲਦਾਰ, ਪਟਵਾਰੀ, ਸੇਵਾ ਕੇਂਦਰ, ਗ੍ਰਾਮ ਪੰਚਾਇਤ, ਡਿਪਟੀ ਕਮਿਸ਼ਨਰ.
Gender: ਲਿੰਗ. Money: ₹6,000; ₹8 ਲੱਖ. September: ਸਤੰਬਰ.

Rythu Bharosa (Rs.12,000 per Acre for Farmers)

Telangana gives farmers Rs.12,000 per acre a year for crop costs, paid as Rs.6,000 per acre before each season (Vanakalam and Yasangi) straight into the farmer's bank account. Rythu Bharosa replaced the old Rythu Bandhu scheme from 26 January 2025. Every pattadar whose farmland is recorded in Bhu Bharati (earlier Dharani) is included automatically, with no new application each season. A new farmer, or one whose money is not coming, gives bank and passbook details to the Agriculture Extension Officer (AEO) of the cluster.
Rs.12,000 per acre a year (Rs.6,000 per acre each season)
Pattadar (land owner) whose farmland is recorded in the Bhu Bharati (earlier Dharani) land records
Tribal farmers holding forest-rights (ROFR) pattas are also eligible
Money is paid only for land fit for farming. House plots, layouts, real-estate ventures, mines, roads and land taken for projects are left out
A bank account in the farmer's own name, linked with Aadhaar
Tenant farmers are not covered. Landless farm labourers have a separate scheme (Indiramma Atmiya Bharosa)
Bank passbook front page with account number and IFSC
Aadhaar consent form, signed (the AEO gives it)
Mutation / Bhu Bharati record if the land was bought or inherited recently

Give the filled Rythu Bharosa Bank Details Collection Form to the Agriculture Extension Officer (AEO) of your cluster at the Rythu Vedika, or at the Mandal Agriculture Office. Attach copies of the pattadar passbook, Aadhaar and bank passbook, and sign the Aadhaar consent form. The AEO checks the details, signs the form and uploads it on the Rythu Bharosa portal. AEO mobile numbers are under Contact Us on rythubharosa.telangana.gov.in.

Get the Bank Details Collection Form from the AEO, or download it. Fill in your name, Aadhaar, passbook number, mobile number and bank details, and sign it.
Give it to the AEO at your Rythu Vedika with copies of the passbook, Aadhaar and bank passbook. The AEO checks and uploads it on the portal.
Before each season the government releases the money, usually to small holdings first and then to larger ones. Rs.6,000 per acre is credited to your account by DBT.
Check the bank SMS or your passbook. If neighbours were paid and you were not, ask the AEO to check your status on the portal. The usual reasons are an Aadhaar-bank mismatch or a closed account.
If the problem stays, complain to the Mandal Agriculture Officer, then to the District Agriculture Officer or the Collector's grievance cell.

Telangana Construction Workers Registration (BOCW Labour Card)
Telangana Building & Other Construction Workers Welfare Board, Labour Department

A construction worker registered with the Telangana Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board gets an identity card and the board's benefits: Rs.6 lakh if the worker dies in an accident, Rs.1 lakh on natural death, up to Rs.5 lakh for permanent disability, Rs.30,000 for the marriage of a woman worker or of up to two daughters, and Rs.30,000 for each of up to two deliveries. Masons, helpers, painters, carpenters, plumbers, electricians, brick-kiln and road workers and over 50 other trades can register. Fill Form XXVII and give it at the Assistant Labour Officer's office with a work certificate and the Rs.50 fee; membership then costs Rs.12 a year.
Rs.6 lakh if the worker dies in an accident; Rs.30,000 each for marriage and for delivery
Works as a mason, helper or coolie, painter, carpenter, plumber, electrician, bar bender or centering worker, or in tiles, road, brick-kiln, quarry or another listed construction trade
Works in Telangana; migrant workers from other states can also register
Keeps membership renewed (Rs.12 a year or Rs.60 for five years) to stay eligible for benefits

Certificate of 90 days' work from the Assistant Labour Officer, a construction workers' union, or a registered builder or establishment

At the office of the Assistant Labour Officer (ALO) for your area, mandal or circle. In Hyderabad, go to the ALO office of your circle. Pay Rs.50 registration plus Rs.12 for one year or Rs.60 for five years. To renew, pay by challan at any SBI branch and give the challan copy to the same ALO. Claim forms for each benefit are on the Downloads page of tbocwwb.telangana.gov.in.

Rajiv Aarogyasri Health Scheme (Aarogyasri Card)
Aarogyasri Health Care Trust, Health, Medical & Family Welfare Department, Telangana

Free treatment worth up to Rs.10 lakh a year per family for serious illnesses and operations, such as heart, cancer, kidney, brain and accident cases, covering about 1,835 listed treatments, at government hospitals and at private hospitals that have joined the scheme (network hospitals) in Telangana. Treatment is cashless: the Aarogyasri Trust pays the hospital, not you. There is no form to fill: your white ration card (Food Security Card) is your proof, and the Aarogyamitra at the hospital desk registers you on the spot.
Up to Rs.10 lakh a year per family, cashless, for listed treatments
Families holding a Telangana Food Security Card (white ration card), or an Aarogyasri health card already issued to the family
Every member named on the card is covered: head of family, spouse, children and dependent parents
Orphan children are being given their own Aarogyasri cards through the Women & Child Welfare Department
Only treatments on the Aarogyasri list are covered, at a government or network hospital. Ordinary OPD visits are not covered
Government employees and pensioners are not covered here. They use the separate Employees Health Scheme (EHS)
Food Security Card (white ration card) or Aarogyasri health card, the original
Aadhaar card of the patient (the original, for fingerprint or face check)
Old prescriptions, scan and test reports, if you have any
Referral letter from a PHC, government hospital or health camp, if you have one

Go to the Aarogyamitra help desk (Aarogyasri counter) at any government hospital (Area, District or Teaching hospital) or at an Aarogyasri network private hospital. The Aarogyamitra at your PHC can tell you which hospitals are in the scheme. Take the original white ration card or Aarogyasri card, the patient's Aadhaar and any old reports. The Aarogyamitra checks the card online, takes the patient's photo and fingerprint, and registers the case. For a listed treatment, you pay nothing at any stage.
Printed on your white ration card. Once the Aarogyamitra types it in, everyone on the card comes up.
Patient name (as on the card)
Must match the name on the ration card. If the spelling differs, show your Aadhaar as well.
The fingerprint or face check is done on this Aadhaar, so bring the original card.
Updates about approval and discharge come to this number.
Say it in your own words. The doctor writes down the illness after checking the patient.
Filled in by the Aarogyamitra according to the department you are sent to.
Keep the white ration card and the patient's Aadhaar ready. If you are not sure a hospital is in Aarogyasri, ask the Aarogyamitra at your PHC or call 104.
At the hospital, go to the Aarogyamitra desk first, not the cash counter. Show the card. The Aarogyamitra registers the patient online, with a photo and fingerprint.
The doctor examines the patient and orders tests. If the treatment is on the list, the hospital asks the Aarogyasri Trust online for approval (pre-authorisation).
Approval usually comes within hours, and at once in an emergency. The Aarogyamitra tells you when it is approved.
The operation, medicines and hospital stay are free. Do not pay any money. If anyone asks you to pay, refuse and call 104.
At discharge, sign the discharge papers and collect your medicines and the date of your follow-up visit. Follow-up check-ups for the same treatment are also free.
Aarogyasri call centre 104; Aarogyasri Health Care Trust, Hyderabad 040-23547107

Your home gets a zero electricity bill for every month it uses 200 units or less. It covers one home connection for each family with a white ration card linked to Aadhaar, and the bill stays in the house owner's name, so tenants get it too. If a month's use goes above 200 units, the whole month's bill must be paid, not only the extra units. Families who applied in Praja Palana were added automatically; others apply at the MPDO or municipal office.
Zero bill for every month the home uses 200 units or less
Family holds a Telangana Food Security Card (white ration card) linked with Aadhaar
One home (domestic) electricity connection per family. The house can be rented
The application is entered in the Praja Palana portal with the ration card and the connection's USC number
The connection is used only for the home. Using it for a shop or business is an offence
Monthly use is 200 units or less. Above 200 units the full bill is payable for that month
Latest electricity bill showing the USC (unique service connection) number
Food Security Card (white ration card)
Aadhaar card of the head of the family
Praja Palana receipt number, if you applied earlier

Give the Praja Palana (Gruha Jyothi) application at the Praja Palana counter in your MPDO office (villages) or the municipal office or GHMC circle office (towns). Attach copies of the white ration card, Aadhaar and the latest electricity bill showing the USC number. If you applied before but still get a bill, ask the same office to correct the ration card or USC number in Praja Palana. Take the receipt and show it at your electricity section office (AE office).
Aadhaar of the head of the family.
From the white ration card. Without it the scheme cannot be linked.
The address where this electricity connection is.
See 'units consumed' on your bill. Only months of 200 units or less get a zero bill.
The USC number printed on the bill, not the meter number. One mistake here and the zero bill does not come.
If you rent, this can be the owner's name. The name on the bill is not changed.
Find the USC number on your latest electricity bill, and keep the white ration card and Aadhaar ready.
Go to the Praja Palana counter at the MPDO or municipal office. Fill the form with the units you use and the USC number, attach copies and take the receipt.
The office enters it in the Praja Palana portal, and the power company links your ration card to your connection.
From the next billing month, the meter reader gives a zero bill whenever the month's use is 200 units or less.
Watch your use. If it crosses 200 units, that whole month's bill must be paid. The zero bill comes back the next month you stay within 200.
Still getting a bill? Take the receipt to your electricity section (AE) office, or call 1912, and ask them to link your connection.
Electricity complaints 1912; TGNPDCL toll free 1800-425-0028; your MPDO or municipal office for the application
Mahalakshmi (Free Bus Travel for Women and Rs.500 Gas Cylinder)
Government of Telangana: TGSRTC (free bus) and Civil Supplies Department (gas subsidy)

Under Mahalakshmi, one of Telangana's six guarantees, since 9 December 2023 women, girls and transgender persons living in Telangana have travelled free in TGSRTC Palle Velugu, Express, City Ordinary and Metro Express buses: show an ID and take the zero ticket. Families with a white ration card who applied through Praja Palana get each LPG cylinder for Rs.500: you pay the full price on delivery and the rest comes back to your bank account. The promised Rs.2,500 a month for women heads of family has not started yet, and there is no application open for it (October 2026).
Free state bus travel for women; LPG cylinder for Rs.500
Free bus: any woman, girl or transgender person living in Telangana, of any age or income, for travel within Telangana
Free bus is valid in Palle Velugu, Express, City Ordinary and Metro Express buses, not in Deluxe, Super Luxury or AC buses
Rs.500 gas: the family holds a Telangana Food Security Card (white ration card)
Rs.500 gas: the family has an active domestic LPG connection and applied for this in Praja Palana or later at the MPDO / municipal office
Rs.500 gas: the number of cylinders is limited to what the family used on average in the last three years
Bus: Aadhaar card or any government photo ID with a Telangana address (voter ID, driving licence)
Gas: Food Security Card (white ration card)
Gas: Aadhaar card of the applicant
Gas: gas consumer book or latest cylinder bill showing the consumer number and agency
Gas: bank passbook of the account linked to the gas connection
Gas: Praja Palana receipt number, if you applied earlier
